title: Portable generator safety
summary: Run it outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house. Never plug it into a wall outlet. Let it cool before refueling.

sources.title: CPSC: Winter Storm May Knock Out Power; CPSC Warns of Deadly Carbon Monoxide and Fire Risks

blocks.text: **Never run a generator inside your home, garage, basement, crawlspace or shed.** Not even with doors and windows open. The carbon monoxide (CO) can kill you in your sleep. Nearly 100 people a year die from generator CO in the U.S.

items: **At least 20 feet** from windows, doors and attached garages.
Not on a porch or in a carport.
Point the exhaust away from the house and any entrance. Close nearby windows and seal nearby vents.
Keep it **dry**. Touching a wet generator can shock you. Follow the maker's weather advice.
Put working CO alarms on every level of your house.

blocks.text: **Never plug a generator into a wall outlet.** This "backfeeds" power into the lines. It can kill utility workers and neighbors, even far from your house.

items: Plug appliances **straight into the generator**, or use heavy-duty, outdoor-rated extension cords.
No cords with exposed wires or worn covers. Don't run cords under rugs or across walkways.
The only safe way to power house wiring is a **transfer switch** installed by a licensed electrician.
Don't run more than the generator's output rating. Power only the essentials.
Turn the generator **off** and let it **cool** before you add fuel. Spilled fuel on hot parts can ignite.
Store gasoline **outdoors** in labeled, non-glass safety containers.
Don't store fuel in a garage that has a fuel-burning appliance. Vapors can travel along the floor and ignite.
Keep a charged, approved fire extinguisher near the generator.

blocks.text: Many parts of a running generator can burn skin. Keep children and pets away. Turn off everything plugged into it before you shut it down.
Read and follow your generator's manual. If a generator makes you feel dizzy, weak, sick or confused, get into fresh air and call 911. See the carbon monoxide guide.
